| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | not-started | 2026-08-07 — D46 recorded, and the trait opt-out D28 left to the implementing slice was REBUILT after the first spelling was found wanting. The marker set on `#Component` — keyed by contract FQN, beside `#traits` — is gone. `#Trait` carries `optional: bool` beside `spec`, `core` gives it NO DEFAULT, the declaring catalog states the posture AS A DEFAULT (`bool | *true` advisory, `bool | *false` load-bearing), and a module overrides it at the attachment site: `#traits: (BackupFQN): Backup & {optional: true}`. WHAT THE FIRST SPELLING GOT WRONG was not the location but the reading of D28's `lives on the demand side` clause: taken as forbidding a field on `#Trait`, it wrote the contract FQN twice and left the trait's own author — the one who knows whether a trait is advisory — unable to say so. Optionality is a property of the (trait, component) PAIR: `backup` on a throwaway cache is advisory, on a database it is the entire point. A default plus an attachment-site override says both; a demand-side-only marker says one. THE DEMAND SIDE STILL WINS, structurally rather than by convention — measured against cue v0.17.1, a module narrowing a DEFAULT is never a conflict while narrowing a CONCRETE value always is, which is the whole reason the catalog must state a default rather than a value. `core` states none of its own because TWO DEFAULTS DO NOT COMPOSE: a catalog restating one against a core default annihilates both and leaves `bool | true | false` — incomplete, defaultless, and reported as `incomplete value bool`, which never says why. THE RULE THE SCHEMA CANNOT CARRY went to a gate. CUE cannot express `you may supply a default here but not a value`, because what separates the two cases is who wrote it; so `#TraitOptionalGate` ships in `core` and `opm catalog publish` unifies every published trait's `optional` against it, refusing an unstated posture and a pinned one. That is 0011 D22's mechanism, not a second one, and 0011's D22 and its `cli-catalog-member-gate` slice now name it. TWO GATE PROPERTIES WORTH CARRYING, both measured: it takes the FIELD, not the trait, because handing it a whole `#Trait` drags that trait's `spec` into concreteness checking and a spec is a schema that must never be concrete; and it must be unified into a NON-HIDDEN value under `cue vet -c`, because `-c` does not check hidden fields and one of the two rules — the unstated posture — is an incomplete value that plain `vet` does not report at all. A gate run without `-c`, or into a hidden slot, enforces half of itself silently. `SPEC.md` gains a section 5 for publish gates, and `#TraitOptionalGate` is tracked. EVERY TRAIT IN BOTH CATALOGS MUST NOW STATE A POSTURE — that is the point of the shape, and it is a required edit landing in `catalogs-identity-authoring`, not here. `#Component` carries no optionality field at all. NOT PUBLISHED — `core-alpha-release` remains the cut point. | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | accepted | minor | not-started | 2026-08-05 — `plan.yaml` gains a structured `decisions` field and the repo gains `task decisions:uncovered`. MEASURED FIRST, because the trigger was a cap firing and the useful question was whether the cap was wrong: across the 27 slices in the two entries with plans, the median `concern` sat at 205 of its 240-rune limit, 15 of 27 were within 40 runes, and up to 41 runes went on an inline decision-citation tail (0011's cli-publish-pipeline, 11 decisions). So the cap was not being abused — it had no headroom, and the pressure was ONE-DIRECTIONAL, since a slice's citation list accretes while its description does not. Nothing parsed those citations. RAISING THE CAP WAS REJECTED as treating the symptom and re-arming it later; the field was carrying two things, a one-line description and a decision index, and only the first is what the thinness rule is about. THE COVERAGE INVERSE IS THE REAL PRIZE: `task decisions:uncovered` reports a decision NO SLICE CARRIES, counting citations across entries so 0011's cli-catalog-member-gate is credited with 0010's D17, D21, D25 and D42. That is the audit 0010's own 2026-08-05 event describes doing BY HAND, which found seven pieces of decided work with no slice — D36's library half being real code whose absence would have shipped a schema whose matching read an emptied field. `task vet` checks every cited number resolves and refuses a decision both carried and listed unsliced; coverage itself is deliberately NOT a gate, since an entry's design is legitimately allowed to run ahead of its plan. THE CHECK PAID FOR ITSELF ON FIRST RUN, twice. It rejected the migration's own output — cli-catalog-member-gate's `(0010 D17, D21, D25, D42)` had been read as one cross-entry ref and three local ones, when 0011 D22 says in its own text that all four are 0010's. Both now carried. SEVEN DECISIONS ARE DELIBERATELY UNSLICED and say why, in a new top-level `unsliced` map: 0010's D2, D7, D16 and D23 (three reversed or superseded by D38, one a decision NOT to add a field) and 0011's D5, D10 and D14 (a reversed namespace half, a registry property gated on the ownerless Zot cutover, and a forward-looking reservation nobody publishes to). | [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
